title: Walk Like This: Stylized Locomotion for Physics- Based Characters through Example-Driven Diffusion
summary: We present a real-time framework for expressive legged locomotion that enables independent control over velocity and style. Unlike existing data-driven controllers, which typically require explicit style labels for training, our method efficiently leverages large-scale unstructured motion data and generalizes to unseen styles.

extra.full_text: We present a real-time framework for expressive legged locomotion that enables independent control over velocity and style. Unlike existing data-driven controllers, which typically require explicit style labels for training, our method efficiently leverages large-scale unstructured motion data and generalizes to unseen styles. We disentangle style from functional locomotion through a tailored sampling strategy used to train a style encoder whose output conditions an autoregressive diffusion model. During inference, the user provides a style reference clip and a joystick velocity command. The diffusion model then generates a kinematic reference tracked by a reinforcement learning controller. To improve user controllability and stylization strength, we propose an attention biasing mechanism and a velocity command correction strategy. We demonstrate our method on a physics-based humanoid character in simulation and on a physical robot, showcasing robust real-time control and continuous style modulation. Publication link: https://la.disneyresearch.com/publication/walk-like-this-stylized-locomotion-for-physics-based-characters-through-example-driven-diffusion

title: Kamino: GPU-based Simulation of Rigid Multi-Body Physics with Kinematic Loops
summary: We present Kamino, a GPU-based physics solver for massively parallel simulations of heterogeneous highly-coupled mechanical systems.

extra.full_text: We present Kamino, a GPU-based physics solver for massively parallel simulations of heterogeneous highly-coupled mechanical systems. Implemented in Python using NVIDIA Warp and integrated into the Newton framework, it enables the application of data-driven methods, such as large-scale reinforcement learning, to complex robotic systems that exhibit strongly coupled kinematic and dynamic constraints such as kinematic loops. The latter are often circumvented by approximating the system's topology as a kinematic tree, and incorporating explicit loop-closure constraints or so-called mimic joints. Kamino aims at alleviating this burden by natively supporting these types of couplings. Moreover, Kamino supports heterogeneous worlds, allowing for batched simulation of structurally diverse robots on a single GPU. At its core lies a state-of-the-art constrained optimization algorithm based on ADMM, which computes constraint forces by solving the constrained rigid multi-body forward dynamics transcribed as a nonlinear complementarity problem. This leads to high-fidelity simulations that resolve contact dynamics without resorting to approximate models that simplify or convexify the problem. We demonstrate RL policy training on a biped with six nested kinematic loops, generating a feasible walking policy while simulating 4,096 parallel environments on a single GPU. Publication link: https://kamino.disneyresearch.com

title: 얀 르쿤의 월드 모델 'H-제파', 단·장기 계획 분리로 로봇 경로 계획 성공률 73% 달성
summary: 기존 월드 모델은 단기 세부 동작과 장기 목표를 하나의 잠재 공간에서 동시에 처리하며 예측 정확도가 떨어지는 한계가 있었다. 얀 르쿤이 참여한 새로운 연구에서는 시간 범위와 추상화 수준을 단계별로 분리한 계층형 월드 모델 ‘H-제파(H-JEPA)’를 해결책으로 제시, 시뮬레이션 미로 탐색 실험에서 단일 계층 모델의 성공률을 18%에서 73%로 높였으며 계획에 필요한 연산량도 줄였다.뉴욕대학교(NYU) AMI 랩을 비롯해 인리아(INRIA Paris), 브라운 대학교 등 글로벌 산학 공동 연구진은 지난 5일(현지시간) 로봇의 장기 목

summary: 미국 로봇 데이터 기업 메카 AI(Mecka AI)가 6000만달러(약 800억원) 규모의 시리즈 B 투자를 유치했다고 최근 밝혔다.이번 투자 라운드는 세쿼이아 캐피털이 주도했으며 엔비디아, 마이크로소프트의 벤처 투자 조직 M12, 퀄컴 벤처스, 삼성 등이 신규 투자자로 참여했다.이번 투자에는 도어대시 창업자 겸 최고경영자(CEO) 토니 쉬(Tony Xu), 서비스나우와 스노우플레이크의 전 CEO 프랭크 슬루트먼(Frank Slootman), 테슬라 옵티머스 사업부를 이끌었던 밀란 코바치(Milan Kovac) 등도 개인 투자자로
